gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's own solar inputs take only 12–60 V while its SolarX 4K add-on needs a string of 150–500 V Voc. That leaves no usable range between 60 and 150 V. Two 37.5 V-Voc rooftop panels in series (75 V) are too high for the Apex and too low for the SolarX 4K, so a whole-home array needs at least 4 such panels in series. It also needs a 600 V / 20 A PV disconnect, which is not in the box.
standout_why: Compared against watthourlab.com/home-backup/transfer-switch-basics (cited, opened 2026-11-13). It covers transfer devices, back-feeding, permits, 120/240 V and L14-30 amps, but it does not cover solar panel voltage limits, neutral bonding, GFCI or warranty. ChatGPT's own answer says only that solar must make enough energy and gives no voltage or string rule. I also opened ankersolix.com/products/f3800-plus-home-backup-kit (ranked, not cited). It warns that going over 165 V can damage the F3800 Plus solar ports, but it says nothing about BLUETTI or a minimum string voltage. Popular Mechanics (cited) blocked WebFetch and my curl needed approval, so I could not check it. The score of 3 assumes Popular Mechanics, a roundup of whole-home power stations, does not state the BLUETTI 60 V / 150 V voltage gap; I have not verified that. The finding decides the set: which charge controller to buy, how many panels in series, and the extra PV disconnect.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W, 120/240 V). It is on the approved awin:bluetti_us program, and BLUETTI sells it with batteries and the SolarX 4K controller as one cart item.
Expansion batteries: 2× BLUETTI B300K. Per BLUETTI's US store listing, this brings the bundle to 8,294.4 Wh, a whole-home-scale capacity.

Solar charge controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K. Rooftop strings above 60 V can't go into the Apex 300's own 12–60 V XT60 inputs, so the SolarX takes 150–500 V Voc and steps it down to 35–58 V, up to 4,000 W.

Rooftop panels: enough residential panels in series to reach at least 150 V Voc (for example, 4× 37.5 V-Voc panels, as Notebookcheck tested) and stay under 500 V. Two in series fit neither the Apex nor the SolarX.
PV disconnect: 600 V / 20 A DC switch or fuse box. Notebookcheck says the SolarX 4K needs one and it is not included.
Home connection: a transfer switch or inlet installed by a licensed electrician. Watt Hour Lab cites OSHA against back-feeding without a transfer switch.

findings.label: Built-in solar input
findings.value: 2× XT60, 12–60 V, max 20 A; up to 2,400 W total
findings.source_title: Bluetti APEX 300 battery storage system review (Notebookcheck, Christian Hintze, 2025-08-10, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Hintze quotes the spec label '2x XT60 (12 - 60 V, max. 20 A)'. The article says the Apex alone takes up to 2,400 W of solar, or up to 4,000 W with the SolarX 4K.

findings.label: Minimum PV string voltage
findings.value: 150 V Voc minimum (Voc range 150–500 V); MPPT 120–450 V; max 20 A from panels; output 35–58 V; max 4,000 W out
findings.source_title: Solar charge controller for rooftop systems with storage: first look at the Bluetti SolarX 4K (Notebookcheck, Christian Hintze, 2025-10-06)
findings.note: Hintze: 'The panels themselves should have an open-circuit voltage between 150 and 500 V and deliver no more than 20 A.' His test ran at about 150 V from several 37.5 V-Voc panels in series, which he calls the minimum. BLUETTI's US store page says 'Supports solar panels from 150 V to 500 V' (read 2026-11-13).

findings.label: Voltage range that works with neither input
findings.value: Strings from just over 60 V to just under 150 V Voc can't charge the Apex 300 directly or through the SolarX 4K
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck SolarX 4K first look + Notebookcheck APEX 300 review
findings.note: My arithmetic from the two Notebookcheck specs. With 37.5 V-Voc panels: 1 in series (37.5 V) fits the Apex XT60 input; 2 (75 V) or 3 (112.5 V) fit neither; 4 (150 V) to 13 (487.5 V) fit the SolarX. Voc rises in cold weather and I found no source for a margin figure, so the 13-panel top end is nominal only.

findings.label: Parts the shopper must buy separately
findings.value: PV disconnect switch rated 600 V / 20 A (not included); a battery-side DC output cable (P090A for Apex 300/B300K) that the reviewer says Bluetti doesn't include, €40 to over €100
findings.note: Named reviewer: Christian Hintze. BLUETTI's US store now lists the SolarX with the adapter cable in two versions: 'Locking Terminal to P090D Adapter Cable (for Single Use)' and 'to XT60 Adapter Cable (for Parallel Use)', both $699. So the cable question now comes down to choosing the right version.

findings.label: Mounting / grid limits
findings.value: Wall-mounted vertically indoors (not weatherproof); off-grid only, does not connect to the grid

findings.label: 240 V output while charging on 120 V AC
findings.value: Not available: 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + 10-Circuit Manual Transfer Switch - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Maker's note. So if you recharge it from a 120 V gas generator during a long outage, 240 V loads such as a well pump or central AC lose power. The Home Backup Kit option showed 'Sold Out' and the page showed no price.

findings.label: Solar input limit
findings.value: 2 inputs, 11–165 V, 17 A max, 1,600 W max each (3,200 W total); 'exceeding 165V may cause damage to the solar input ports'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + 10-Circuit Manual Transfer Switch - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Maker's spec and warning. With 37.5 V-Voc panels, 4 in series is 150 V; 5 (187.5 V) would go over the limit.

findings.label: Home connection rule
findings.value: A generator must never be attached directly to a building's wiring unless a qualified electrician has installed a transfer switch; do not back-feed through an outlet
findings.source_title: Home Backup Batteries and Transfer Switch Basics (Watt Hour Lab)
findings.note: The rival page cites OSHA. It also gives L14-30R limits: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 16.7 A, Anker F3800 Plus 25 A.
